content.text: I've read the whole codebase: vanilla JS with Tailwind v4 and FFmpeg.wasm, about 2.7k lines. A few choices here would really change the plan, so I'll check them with you before designing.

questions.question: What visual direction should the revamp take?

options.label: Minimal & refined (Recommended)
options.description: Linear/Vercel-style: neutral palette with a single accent, crisp SVG icons, subtle borders, generous spacing. Feels like a polished modern tool.

options.label: Pro editor
options.description: Photopea/Figma-style: dark and dense, docked panels, compact controls, focused on getting a lot done on screen.

options.label: Friendly & playful
options.description: Rounded, colorful, emoji-forward, Slack-like warmth. More personality, less tool-like.

questions.question: What do people mainly use this app for?

options.label: Both equally
options.description: Keep the general editor and Slack export as peers. Slack export stays a prominent export option.

options.label: Mostly Slack emoji
options.description: Make 'Slack emoji' a first-class mode: a live 128 KB budget meter, a square-crop preview, and batch as a headline feature.

options.label: Mostly general editing
options.description: A general-purpose GIF editor where Slack is one export preset among others.

questions.question: Which UX upgrades should be in scope? (A responsive layout, an SVG icon set, better toasts, filenames kept on download, and bug fixes are included either way.)

options.label: Live previews
options.description: Filter effects show live on the preview, trim uses a visual dual-handle timeline, crop works on touch, and a before/after compare toggle with size delta.

options.label: Instant undo/redo
options.description: Replace the slow FFmpeg replay undo with snapshot history: instant undo/redo plus a clickable history list. This also fixes a bug where undo silently drops frame edits.

options.label: Playback controls
options.description: Play/pause, step frame by frame, scrub, and zoom (fit/100%/pixelated) on a checkerboard background. Uses the WebCodecs ImageDecoder API.

options.label: Power-user flow
options.description: Drop or paste a GIF anywhere at any time, keyboard shortcuts (tool hotkeys, redo, Esc, Ctrl+S) with a '?' cheat sheet, and the engine preloads in the background instead of behind a blocking modal.

input.content: # GIF Editor — UI/UX revamp (branch `ui-improvements`) ## Context The app works, but it feels like a prototype: - Emoji icons and ad-hoc Tailwind classes repeated in every tool. - A full-screen blocking modal for every operation and for engine loading. - Undo is slow: it replays FFmpeg operations. It is also buggy: undo after a Frames edit silently drops that edit, because `replayOperation` has no `frames` case. - No way to pause or scrub the GIF. - Number-only trim inputs. - Mouse-only crop. - Ctrl+Z only, and it hijacks inputs. - Every download is named `edited.gif`. The user asked for a revamp of the whole UI and UX. Choices they confirmed: - **Visual direction:** friendly and playful. - **Use case:** general editing and Slack export are **equal peers**. - **In scope:** live previews, instant undo/redo, playback controls, power-user flow. Stack stays the same: vanilla JS ES modules, Tailwind v4, FFmpeg.wasm, Vite. No framework migration. ## Design direction: "friendly and playful" - **Tokens:** Tailwind v4 `@theme` semantic colors (`surface`, `surface-2`, `ink`, `muted`, `line`, `accent` plus per-tool accent hues) backed by CSS vars, with `@custom-variant dark`. These replace the `t-*` helper classes in `src/styles/custom.css`. - **Theme:** defaults to the system theme. The toggle cycles light → dark → system and is stored in localStorage. - **Shapes and type:** large radii (`rounded-2xl`), soft shadows, springy micro-animations (scale on press, bounce on drop). Animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **Font:** a rounded display font, self-hosted via `@fontsource-variable/nunito`. Google Fonts would be blocked by COEP `require-corp`. - **Icons:** a small inlined SVG set (Lucide paths, ISC) in `src/ui/icons.js`, each tool with its own color chip. Emoji are kept only as personality accents in empty states, not as functional icons. - **Layout:** - **Desktop:** header, left tool rail, center stage, right options panel. - **Mobile:** stage on top, a scrollable tool-chip bar at the bottom, and options in a bottom sheet. ## Implementation (in order; one commit per step) ### 1. Foundation - `src/styles/custom.css`: rewrite as the token system, plus a checkerboard utility, slider/segmented/button styles, and focus rings. Keep the existing WCAG contrast notes. - `src/ui/icons.js` (new): `icon(name, cls)` returns an SVG string. - `src/ui/components.js` (new): small HTML-string helpers used by every tool panel: - `button({variant, icon, label})` - `sliderField({id, label, min, max, step, value, format})` - `segmented({id, options})` - `numberField` - `panelHeader({title, icon, color, hint})` This removes the duplicated class strings in the `src/tools/*.js` panels. - `index.html`: new shell with these parts: - header: logo, filename chip, undo/redo, Export menu, theme, GitHub - landing - editor (tool rail, stage, options panel, history) - batch view - toast region - `` elements for shortcuts The unsupported-browser banner stays. ### 2. State and history: instant undo/redo - `src/utils/state.js`: - Replace `operations`/`checkpoints`/`pushOperation`/`popOperation` with snapshot history `{ entries: [{label, gif, meta}], index }`. - New functions: `commit(label, gif)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `jumpTo(i)`. - Cap at about 30 entries or about 256 MB total, dropping the oldest. Entry 0 (the original) is always kept. - `src/main.js`: delete `replayOperation` and the checkpoint undo logic. Revert becomes `jumpTo(0)`. - `src/components/history.js` (new): a clickable history list in the options panel, plus undo/redo buttons in the header with disabled states. ### 3. Shared tool runner and tool registry - `src/tools/shared.js`: add `runFFmpegJob({label, inputs, commands, output, cleanup})`. It wraps the write → exec (one or more passes) → read → delete pattern that every tool currently repeats. Wire it to `commit()`, toasts and progress. - `src/components/toolbar.js`: turn the hardcoded `tools` array into a registry. Each tool registers `{id, label, icon, color, hotkey, render(panel), enter(), exit()}`. `enter`/`exit` let tools set up and tear down live previews and overlays, which replaces the crop-canvas and frame-strip special cases in `selectTool`. - Each `src/tools/*.js` file is migrated to the registry and the shared runner, which shrinks it noticeably. ### 4. Stage: player, zoom, compare, progress - `src/components/player.js` (new): - **Playback:** a canvas player using WebCodecs `ImageDecoder`, with play/pause, frame step, a scrubber, a frame counter, and a playback-rate hook. - **Fallback:** if `ImageDecoder` isn't available, it shows a plain `` and hides the playback controls. - **Zoom:** Fit, 100%, and +/- zoom, with `image-rendering: pixelated` above 100%, on a checkerboard background. - **Compare:** a "Compare" control that you hold, or toggle with `\`, shows the original (entry 0) against the current GIF. The metadata bar shows the size delta, e.g. `412 KB → 188 KB (−54%)`. - `src/ffmpeg/engine.js`: - **Preload:** the engine starts loading in the background as soon as a GIF loads. - **Status pill:** loading progress is published to state (`engine: {status, pct}`) and shown as a header pill instead of the `ffmpeg-loader` modal. The pill blocks only if you apply a tool before the engine is ready. - **Job progress:** wire `ffmpeg.on('progress')` into the job overlay, which now covers only the stage, not the whole app. It falls back to an indeterminate bar. ### 5. Tool panels with live previews - **Filters:** live CSS `filter` approximation on the stage while you drag the sliders, labelled "preview ≈". Presets become visual swatch thumbnails. - **Speed:** a live preview through the player's playback rate. It shows the new duration. - **Reverse:** a "Preview" button that plays the decoded frames backwards before you apply. - **Trim:** `src/components/trim-timeline.js` (new) is a dual-handle range over a filmstrip, using player frames or delay-proportional segments. It snaps to frame boundaries using `meta.delays` and keeps synced numeric inputs. - **Crop:** - Switch to pointer events so touch works. - Fix the `window` resize listener, which leaks on every render. - Draw against the player canvas. - Add edge handles and a rule-of-thirds grid. - Ratio presets as segmented controls, highlighted when active. - **Compress:** fix the FPS slider (`min="1" value="0"` mismatch → `min="0"`). Add quick presets (Light / Balanced / Tiny). - **Resize:** a proper lock toggle button. Presets as segmented controls, plus a "Fit 128" preset. - **Frames:** - Prefill the output FPS from the GIF's real fps instead of a hardcoded 10. - Bigger thumbnails, with multi-select delete and keyboard reorder. - Revoke the frame URLs on tool exit (they currently leak). ### 6. Export, landing, batch - **Export:** a header split button. The primary action is Download. The menu holds "Slack emoji" and a live 128 KB budget hint. Downloads use the original name: `cat.gif` becomes `cat-edited.gif` (fix in `src/components/export-panel.js`, using `fileName` from state). - **Landing:** a playful hero with an animated drop target and two equal cards ("Edit a GIF" / "Batch Slack emoji"). It also carries a privacy line ("never leaves your device") and a paste hint. - **Batch:** a revamp of `src/components/batch.js`: - per-card status pills with spinners - an overall progress bar - per-item download and before/after size - a "Download .zip" button - existing logic kept: `uniqueName`, `escapeHtml`, `zipSync` with level 0 - **Toasts:** move toasts to bottom-center, with icons, a close button, and an `aria-live` region kept. ### 7. Power-user flow - `src/components/shortcuts.js` (new): - `1–8` select a tool, `Esc` closes the tool, `Space` plays/pauses. - `,` and `.` step frames, `⌘/Ctrl+Z` undoes, `⌘/Ctrl+Shift+Z` redoes, `⌘/Ctrl+S` downloads. - `\` compares, `?` opens the cheat-sheet ``. - Shortcuts are ignored while focus is in an input. - Drop or paste (Ctrl+V) a GIF anywhere, at any time, through a full-window drop overlay. One GIF replaces the current one, after confirming if there is history. Several GIFs open batch. `filterGifs`/`openBatch` from `batch.js` are reused. - README: update the Features list and add a Shortcuts section. ## Reused as-is - `src/ffmpeg/commands.js`, all builders - `src/tools/slack-emoji.js` - `src/utils/gif-info.js`, whose `delays` feed the trim timeline and fps - `src/utils/file-utils.js` - `filterGifs` / `uniqueName` in `src/components/batch.js` - the IndexedDB WASM cache in `engine.js` ## Verification No test suite exists, so verification is build checks plus driving the app in a browser: 1. **Build:** `npm run build` succeeds with no warnings about missing modules. 2. **Drive the app:** `npm run dev`, then use the `run` / claude-in-chrome skills. - **Landing:** load a GIF via click, drag-drop and paste. - **Engine pill:** the pill shows progress without blocking. - **Tools:** apply every tool. Live previews react while dragging, and crop works with a touch emulator. - **History:** undo/redo is instant and correct after a Frames edit (the regression check for the old bug). Clicking history entries jumps between states, and Compare shows the original. - **Player:** play/pause, step, scrub, and zoom up to pixelated 400%. - **Export:** Download produces `-edited.gif`. Slack export lands at ≤128 KB. - **Batch:** drop 3 or more GIFs. Statuses and progress update, and the zip contains the original names. - **Shortcuts:** every key works, `?` opens the dialog, and shortcuts are inert while typing in inputs. 3. **Theme and responsive:** light, dark and system themes. A 375px-wide viewport (bottom sheet, no horizontal scroll). Keyboard-only navigation with visible focus. 4. **Fallback:** Firefox, or with `ImageDecoder` stubbed out. The `` fallback renders and playback controls hide cleanly.
